title: Federated Monitoring Architecture: Privacy-Preserving AI Oversight via Federated Learning
original_idea: Simulate 3 organizations each with 30 benign trajectories. Implement federated averaging for shared anomaly detector training. Compare detection AUC to centrally-trained and per-organization local monitors. Measure privacy benefit vs performance cost.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Reasonable theory about privacy constraints in monitoring deployment. Safety-relevant but the connection is indirect: federated learning is about deployment practicality rather than fundamental monitoring capability.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Federated learning implementation requires understanding distributed training, aggregation protocols, and frameworks like PySyft/Flower. This is significantly beyond beginner level. Even with existing frameworks, setup is complex within 30hrs.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three training paradigms to compare (federated, centralized, local) with dataset splitting and federated infrastructure setup. Moderately scoped but the infrastructure burden makes it feel broad.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
